R345.note: Per-category method allowlist in resolve() is the right shape for a variable-method dispatch sink; 'email.send' still works, the dead 'handle' default fails the same way it did before, and the new RuntimeException for unknown verbs is stated.

R346.note: Encoding &, ", <, > for the double-quoted title attribute closes the breakout while keeping DOMPurify output in the body, but it re-encodes DOMPurify's already-serialized entities, so a bio like 'Tom & Jerry' now tooltips as 'Tom & Jerry' where the original showed 'Tom & Jerry' - an unstated visible change.

R347.note: setSecure(false) to setSecure(true) is the whole fix; nothing else changes (the response text still says 'secure flag set to: false', but that string is unchanged from the original).

R348.note: Sort is used only as a key into a server-side map of column names with account_id/status still bound; the silent fallback of unknown keys to created_at is a restriction the contract calls for and is stated plainly in the write-up (note 'created_at DESC' style direction suffixes are no longer honoured).

R349.note: Exact-match replaces the prefix check, but the added className.startsWith("[") allows every array class of any length (the original rejected all arrays), so a class outside the explicit set is still constructed and an unbounded primitive array allocation is now possible; the two allowlisted report class names are invented rather than flagged as placeholders for the real set, and the write-up's claim that null-class handling was changed is false (original already returned UNDECIDED).

R350.note: SecureRandom.nextBytes over 16 bytes replaces Math.random for the remember-me token; the token format change is inherent and stated, the value is stored and compared consistently, and standard Base64 characters are valid cookie-octets (the explanation's 'URL-safe' claim is inaccurate but harmless).

R351.note: html.EscapeString on customerNote closes the sink; escaping ticketID as well is stated extra hardening that blocks no legitimate use.

R352.note: The slot-table/generation redesign stops the freed pointer being dereferenced in this main(), but connection_allocate() resets generation to 0 on reuse, so a stale queued context matches a re-allocated slot and fires against the wrong live connection - the exact ABA case the write-up claims is prevented; the fix also rewrites the public signatures of enqueue_completion and handle_connection_reset and adds stderr output, well beyond the sink, and connection_allocate() ignores malloc failure.

R353.note: Three static @Select methods selected by a switch remove ${} entirely with tenantId still bound; the IllegalArgumentException for unknown keys is the restriction the contract calls for and is stated (note the selected 'id' column and any direction suffix are not offered as sort keys).

R354.note: The supplied files are byte-identical to the case, which already used prepareStatement with ? and setString, so the resulting code has no injection vector and nothing else changes; the write-up misdescribes this unchanged code as a remediation rather than saying no change was needed.
